bundle.title: Show what a priority's outreach brought back, behind serve-citizen-panels
bundle.body:
An official working a priority could send texts, calls and door knocks about it, but had no one place to see what people said back across all of them. The agents were no better off: when a check went out, the priority agent and the Chief of Staff asked the official how many replied and what they said, when the answers were already in our records.

This pools every send linked to a priority into one feedback synthesis run (a new `priority` scope on `FeedbackSynthesisRun`), so a door walk after a text feeds the same themes. A new Constituent feedback page under "Where this stands" shows who answered and on which channel, how many joined the citizens' panel, the pooled themes, a coarse heat grid of where answers came from, and how those neighborhoods compare with the district. The agents get `read_outreach_feedback`, which returns replies and notes in people's words plus the themes, and their prompts now tell them to read it rather than ask.

Everything a user can see is behind `serve-citizen-panels`: the link renders only with the flag on, the page reads the flag server-side and 404s when off, `GET /v1/priorities/:id/results` 404s for a user without the flag, and `read_outreach_feedback` (with the prompt lines that mention it) registers only when the flag is on for the chatting user.

Priority synthesis runs are not gated on the panel flag. They start when a send on a priority finishes, behind the existing issue capture rollout like effort runs, and write themes with no tags, so with the surfaces off nothing they write is visible anywhere.

The census comparison still reads `SampleCensusComposition`. Swapping that binding for the real district and block group tables has to happen before the flag reaches an official.

The citizens' panel first checks, panel rotation, and the proposal refusal handling stay out of this PR; they ship next.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches feedback synthesis ingest/scoping, new API surface for respondent locations and demographics, and LLM tools that expose constituent verbatims—feature-flagged but meaningful data-handling and pipeline behavior changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **pooled priority feedback**: a new `priority` synthesis scope on `FeedbackSynthesisRun` (with `priority_id` and migration) rolls up every Serve send on a priority into one theme run, triggered when sends finish or when a send is re-summarized. Ingest scopes members across those sends and skips tag application for pooled runs.
> 
> Exposes **`GET /v1/priorities/:id/results`** and shared **`PriorityResults`** contracts: per-send reach/responses, respondent totals (including civic panel joins), pooled themes with a `summarizing` flag, privacy-rounded map points, and district comparison bars (sample census via `SampleCensusComposition` until real ACS ships).
> 
> **Web:** Constituent feedback at `/dashboard/priorities/[id]/results` plus a rail link, heat grid map, and representation UI—all gated on **`serve-citizen-panels`** (404 when off, matching the API).
> 
> **Agents:** New **`read_outreach_feedback`** tool on priority flow and Chief of Staff (same flag), backed by `PriorityFlowOutreachService.feedbackFor` / `pooledThemes`, with prompt updates to read replies instead of asking the official.
> 
> Priority synthesis itself still rolls out behind **issue capture**, not the panel flag—so themes can be computed even when the new surfaces are hidden.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 410d58f4ee07a24eb38ef9ad3b51664fc7bcd238. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+import { z } from 'zod'
+
+// What a priority's outreach brought back, pooled across every send linked to
+// it (GET /v1/priorities/:id/results): the reach, the themes across every
+// channel, where respondents live, and how those places compare with the
+// district.
+
+export const PRIORITY_RESULTS_CHANNELS = [
+  'text',
+  'phoneBanking',
+  'doorKnocking',
+  'social',
+] as const
+export const PriorityResultsChannelSchema = z.enum(PRIORITY_RESULTS_CHANNELS)
+export type PriorityResultsChannel = z.infer<
+  typeof PriorityResultsChannelSchema
+>
+
+export const PriorityResultsSendSchema = z.object({
+  outreachId: z.number().int(),
+  name: z.string().nullable(),
+  channel: PriorityResultsChannelSchema,
+  date: z.string().nullable(),
+  // People the send reached (texted, called, knocked). Null for a post,
+  // which has no audience to count.
+  reached: z.number().int().nullable(),
+  responded: z.number().int().nullable(),
+})
+export type PriorityResultsSend = z.infer<typeof PriorityResultsSendSchema>
+
+// One respondent's home, rounded to about 100m so the map shows where people
+// are without pinning anyone's house. No ids ride with it.
+export const PriorityResultsPointSchema = z.object({
+  lat: z.number(),
+  lng: z.number(),
+})
+
+export const REPRESENTATION_DIMENSIONS = [
+  'age',
+  'race',
+  'education',
+  'income',
+  'housing',
+  'poverty',
+] as const
+export const RepresentationDimensionSchema = z.enum(REPRESENTATION_DIMENSIONS)
+export type RepresentationDimension = z.infer<
+  typeof RepresentationDimensionSchema
+>
+
+export const RepresentationGroupSchema = z.object({
+  dimension: RepresentationDimensionSchema,
+  key: z.string(),
+  label: z.string(),
+  // Shares are fractions, 0.25 is 25%. The respondent side is each
+  // respondent's census block group composition, averaged, so both sides
+  // read the same census source.
+  respondentShare: z.number(),
+  districtShare: z.number(),
+})
+export type RepresentationGroup = z.infer<typeof RepresentationGroupSchema>
+
+export const PriorityRepresentationSchema = z.object({
+  // `sample` is stand-in figures shaped like the census tables, shown with a
+  // label until the real district and block group demographics are readable.
+  source: z.enum(['sample', 'census']),
+  respondentCount: z.number().int(),
+  groups: z.array(RepresentationGroupSchema),
+})
+export type PriorityRepresentation = z.infer<
+  typeof PriorityRepresentationSchema
+>
+
+// One theme from the priority's latest pooled synthesis run. `people` is
+// distinct people counted now: confirmed notes and replies, so someone who
+// texted twice counts once.
+export const PriorityThemeSchema = z.object({
+  id: z.string(),
+  title: z.string(),
+  summary: z.string(),
+  people: z.number().int(),
+})
+export type PriorityTheme = z.infer<typeof PriorityThemeSchema>
+
+export const PriorityResultsSchema = z.object({
+  priorityId: z.string(),
+  sends: z.array(PriorityResultsSendSchema),
+  respondents: z.object({
+    total: z.number().int(),
+    byChannel: z.object({
+      text: z.number().int(),
+      phoneBanking: z.number().int(),
+      doorKnocking: z.number().int(),
+    }),
+    joinedCivicPanel: z.number().int(),
+  }),
+  themes: z.array(PriorityThemeSchema),
+  // A pooled run is in flight: the themes shown are the previous run's.
+  summarizing: z.boolean(),
+  points: z.array(PriorityResultsPointSchema),
+  // Null below the minimum number of respondents, where a comparison would
+  // say more about chance than about who was heard.
+  representation: PriorityRepresentationSchema.nullable(),
+})
+export type PriorityResults = z.infer<typeof PriorityResultsSchema>
+
+export const MIN_RESPONDENTS_FOR_REPRESENTATION = 10

+import { z } from 'zod'
+import type { LlmStreamTool } from '@/llm/services/llm.service'
+import {
+  OutreachFeedback,
+  PooledTheme,
+  PriorityFlowOutreachService,
+} from '../priority-flow/services/priorityFlowOutreach.service'
+
+const readOutreachFeedbackInput = z.object({
+  outreachId: z
+    .number()
+    .int()
+    .optional()
+    .describe('One send, from read_past_outreach. Omit for every send.'),
+})
+
+export const buildReadOutreachFeedbackTool = (deps: {
+  outreach: PriorityFlowOutreachService
+  priorityId: string | null
+  organizationSlug: string
+}): LlmStreamTool<typeof readOutreachFeedbackInput> => ({
+  description:
+    'Read what came back from the office’s sends in people’s own words: ' +
+    'each text reply (opt-outs left out), each door or call note with the ' +
+    'issues and stances pulled from it, and the themes the latest summary ' +
+    'found. ' +
+    (deps.priorityId === null
+      ? 'Without an outreachId it reads the office’s most recent sends. '
+      : 'Without an outreachId it reads every send for this priority, and ' +
+        'priorityThemes are the themes across all of them, texts, calls ' +
+        'and doors together; lead with those. ') +
+    'Call it before you say anything about what constituents said, and ' +
+    'never ask the official how many replied or what people said: read it ' +
+    'here. Quote people’s words when they make the point, and say how many ' +
+    'people a theme covers. A door or call note that is not confirmed is a ' +
+    'volunteer’s account the official has not reviewed yet.',
+  inputSchema: readOutreachFeedbackInput,
+  execute: async ({
+    outreachId,
+  }): Promise<{
+    priorityThemes: PooledTheme[]
+    sends: OutreachFeedback[]
+  }> => ({
+    priorityThemes:
+      deps.priorityId === null
+        ? []
+        : await deps.outreach.pooledThemes(
+            deps.organizationSlug,
+            deps.priorityId,
+          ),
+    sends: await deps.outreach.feedbackFor(deps.organizationSlug, {
+      priorityId: deps.priorityId,
+      outreachId,
+    }),
+  }),
+})

+import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'
+import { ACS_COUNT_KEYS, type AcsCounts } from '../util/representation.util'
+
+export interface CensusRespondent {
+  personId: string
+  lat: number
+  lng: number
+}
+
+export interface CensusComposition {
+  source: 'sample' | 'census'
+  district: AcsCounts
+  // One entry per respondent whose block group was found, in any order.
+  respondentBlockGroups: AcsCounts[]
+}
+
+// Where district and block group demographics come from. The real reader
+// needs gp-data-platform's district ACS columns and block group table in
+// mart_gp_api, plus each person's block group geoid on the people read; until
+// those ship, SampleCensusComposition stands in with figures shaped exactly
+// like them, and the page labels them as sample data.
+export interface CensusCompositionSource {
+  compose(input: {
+    districtKey: string
+    respondents: CensusRespondent[]
+  }): Promise<CensusComposition | null>
+}
+
+export const CENSUS_COMPOSITION_SOURCE = 'CensusCompositionSource'
+
+const SAMPLE_BLOCK_GROUPS = 60
+// About 1.4 km on a side: neighbors share a sample block group, so a send
+// that only reached one part of town shows up as a skew.
+const CELLS_PER_DEGREE = 70
+
+const hash = (text: string): number => {
+  let h = 2166136261
+  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
+    h ^= text.charCodeAt(i)
+    h = Math.imul(h, 16777619)
+  }
+  return h >>> 0
+}
+
+// mulberry32: small, seeded, and the same on every run, so a page reload
+// never reshuffles the sample.
+const seeded = (seed: number) => () => {
+  let t = (seed += 0x6d2b79f5)
+  t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1)
+  t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61)
+  return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
+}
+
+const sampleBlockGroup = (random: () => number): AcsCounts => {
+  const population = 600 + Math.round(random() * 1800)
+  // Shares a total out by weight, keyed so each part keeps its name.
+  const split = <K extends string>(
+    total: number,
+    weights: Record<K, number>,
+  ): ((key: K) => number) => {
+    const sum = Object.values<number>(weights).reduce((a, w) => a + w, 0)
+    return (key) => Math.round((total * weights[key]) / sum)
+  }
+  const under18 = Math.round(population * (0.12 + random() * 0.18))
+  const over65 = Math.round(population * (0.08 + random() * 0.22))
+  const race = split(population, {
+    white: 3 + random() * 8,
+    black: random() * 3,
+    hispanic: random() * 2.5,
+    asian: random() * 0.8,
+    native: random() * 0.15,
+    other: random() * 0.6,
+  })
+  const adults25 = Math.round(population * (0.6 + random() * 0.15))
+  const hs = Math.round(adults25 * (0.75 + random() * 0.22))
+  const bachelors = Math.round(hs * (0.2 + random() * 0.55))
+  const households = Math.round(population / (1.9 + random() * 0.9))
+  const owners = Math.round(households * (0.25 + random() * 0.6))
+  const belowPoverty = Math.round(population * (0.04 + random() * 0.24))
+  const income = split(households, {
+    under25k: 1 + random() * 3,
+    from25k: 1 + random() * 2,
+    from50k: 1 + random() * 2,
+    from75k: 0.5 + random() * 1.5,
+    from100k: 0.3 + random() * 1.5,
+    from150k: 0.2 + random() * 1.8,
+  })
+  return {
+    totalPopulation: population,
+    populationUnder18: under18,
+    population65Plus: over65,
+    populationRaceUniverse: population,
+    populationWhiteNh: race('white'),
+    populationBlackNh: race('black'),
+    populationNativeAmericanNh: race('native'),
+    populationAsianNh: race('asian'),
+    populationOtherNh: race('other'),
+    populationHispanic: race('hispanic'),
+    population25Plus: adults25,
+    populationHsOrHigher: hs,
+    populationBachelorsOrHigher: bachelors,
+    households,
+    ownerOccupiedHouseholds: owners,
+    populationPovertyUniverse: population,
+    populationBelowPoverty: belowPoverty,
+    householdsIncomeUniverse: households,
+    householdsIncomeUnder25k: income('under25k'),
+    householdsIncome25kTo50k: income('from25k'),
+    householdsIncome50kTo75k: income('from50k'),
+    householdsIncome75kTo100k: income('from75k'),
+    householdsIncome100kTo150k: income('from100k'),
+    householdsIncome150kPlus: income('from150k'),
+  }
+}
+
+const sumCounts = (first: AcsCounts, rest: AcsCounts[]): AcsCounts => {
+  const total = { ...first }
+  for (const group of rest) {
+    for (const key of ACS_COUNT_KEYS) total[key] += group[key]
+  }
+  return total
+}
+
+@Injectable()
+export class SampleCensusComposition implements CensusCompositionSource {
+  async compose(input: {
+    districtKey: string
+    respondents: CensusRespondent[]
+  }): Promise<CensusComposition> {
+    const random = seeded(hash(input.districtKey))
+    const first = sampleBlockGroup(random)
+    const blockGroups = [
+      first,
+      ...Array.from({ length: SAMPLE_BLOCK_GROUPS - 1 }, () =>
+        sampleBlockGroup(random),
+      ),
+    ]
+    const cellOf = ({ lat, lng }: CensusRespondent): number =>
+      hash(
+        `${Math.floor(lat * CELLS_PER_DEGREE)}:${Math.floor(lng * CELLS_PER_DEGREE)}`,
+      ) % SAMPLE_BLOCK_GROUPS
+    return {
+      source: 'sample',
+      district: sumCounts(first, blockGroups.slice(1)),
+      respondentBlockGroups: input.respondents.map(
+        (respondent) => blockGroups[cellOf(respondent)] ?? first,
+      ),
+    }
+  }
+}

+import { Inject, Injectable, NotFoundException } from '@nestjs/common'
+import { ModuleRef } from '@nestjs/core'
+import {
+  MIN_RESPONDENTS_FOR_REPRESENTATION,
+  type PriorityResults,
+  type PriorityResultsChannel,
+  type PriorityResultsSend,
+  type PriorityTheme,
+} from '@goodparty_org/contracts'
+import {
+  ContactStatusField,
+  ElectedOffice,
+  Outreach,
+  OutreachType,
+  PollIndividualMessageSender,
+  Prisma,
+  SynthesisRunStatus,
+  SynthesisScope,
+} from '../../generated/prisma'
+import { createPrismaBase, MODELS } from '@/prisma/util/prisma.util'
+import { ContactsService } from '@/contacts/services/contacts.service'
+import { computeRepresentation } from '../util/representation.util'
+import {
+  CENSUS_COMPOSITION_SOURCE,
+  type CensusCompositionSource,
+} from './censusComposition'
+
+const CHANNEL_BY_TYPE: Partial<Record<OutreachType, PriorityResultsChannel>> = {
+  [OutreachType.text]: 'text',
+  [OutreachType.nativePhoneBanking]: 'phoneBanking',
+  [OutreachType.nativeDoorKnocking]: 'doorKnocking',
+  [OutreachType.socialMedia]: 'social',
+}
+
+// ~100m. Enough to see which blocks answered, not enough to find a house.
+const roundCoordinate = (value: number): number =>
+  Math.round(value * 1000) / 1000
+
+interface SendRespondents {
+  send: PriorityResultsSend
+  respondentIds: string[]
+}
+
+@Injectable()
+export class PriorityResultsService extends createPrismaBase(MODELS.Priority) {
+  constructor(
+    private readonly moduleRef: ModuleRef,
+    @Inject(CENSUS_COMPOSITION_SOURCE)
+    private readonly census: CensusCompositionSource,
+  ) {
+    super()
+  }
+
+  async resultsFor(
+    electedOffice: ElectedOffice,
+    priorityId: string,
+  ): Promise<PriorityResults> {
+    const priority = await this.model.findFirst({
+      where: { id: priorityId, electedOfficeId: electedOffice.id },
+      select: { id: true },
+    })
+    if (!priority) throw new NotFoundException('Priority not found')
+
+    const organizationSlug = electedOffice.organizationSlug
+    const outreaches = await this.client.outreach.findMany({
+      where: {
+        priorityId,
+        organizationSlug,
+        campaignId: null,
+        status: { notIn: ['pending_payment', 'draft', 'canceled'] },
+      },
+      orderBy: { createdAt: 'asc' },
+    })
+
+    const perSend = await Promise.all(
+      outreaches.flatMap((outreach) => {
+        const channel = CHANNEL_BY_TYPE[outreach.outreachType]
+        return channel ? [this.respondentsFor(outreach, channel)] : []
+      }),
+    )
+
+    const byChannel = { text: 0, phoneBanking: 0, doorKnocking: 0 }
+    const respondentIds = new Set<string>()
+    for (const { send, respondentIds: ids } of perSend) {
+      if (send.channel !== 'social') byChannel[send.channel] += ids.length
+      for (const id of ids) respondentIds.add(id)
+    }
+    const ids = [...respondentIds]
+
+    const joinedCivicPanel =
+      ids.length === 0
+        ? 0
+        : await this.client.contactCurrentStatus.count({
+            where: {
+              organizationSlug,
+              field: ContactStatusField.civic_panel,
+              value: 'member',
+              personId: { in: ids },
+            },
+          })
+
+    const organization = await this.client.organization.findUniqueOrThrow({
+      where: { slug: organizationSlug },
+    })
+    const { points } = await this.resolveContacts().pointsForPeople(
+      ids,
+      organization,
+    )
+
+    const composition =
+      points.length >= MIN_RESPONDENTS_FOR_REPRESENTATION
+        ? await this.census.compose({
+            districtKey: organizationSlug,
+            respondents: points.map(({ id, lat, lng }) => ({
+              personId: id,
+              lat,
+              lng,
+            })),
+          })
+        : null
+
+    const { themes, summarizing } = await this.pooledThemes(
+      organizationSlug,
+      priorityId,
+    )
+
+    return {
+      priorityId,
+      sends: perSend.map(({ send }) => send),
+      respondents: { total: ids.length, byChannel, joinedCivicPanel },
+      themes,
+      summarizing,
+      points: points.map(({ lat, lng }) => ({
+        lat: roundCoordinate(lat),
+        lng: roundCoordinate(lng),
+      })),
+      representation: composition && {
+        source: composition.source,
+        respondentCount: composition.respondentBlockGroups.length,
+        groups: computeRepresentation(
+          composition.district,
+          composition.respondentBlockGroups,
+        ),
+      },
+    }
+  }
+
+  // The latest completed pooled run's themes. A run in flight leaves the
+  // previous themes up, the way an effort's report does.
+  private async pooledThemes(
+    organizationSlug: string,
+    priorityId: string,
+  ): Promise<{ themes: PriorityTheme[]; summarizing: boolean }> {
+    const scope = {
+      organizationSlug,
+      priorityId,
+      scope: SynthesisScope.priority,
+    }
+    const [latest, running] = await Promise.all([
+      this.client.feedbackSynthesisRun.findFirst({
+        where: { ...scope, status: SynthesisRunStatus.completed },
+        orderBy: { completedAt: Prisma.SortOrder.desc },
+        select: {
+          themes: {
+            orderBy: { rank: Prisma.SortOrder.asc },
+            select: {
+              id: true,
+              title: true,
+              summary: true,
+              members: {
+                where: {
+                  OR: [
+                    { feedback: { confirmedAt: { not: null } } },
+                    { textReplyId: { not: null } },
+                  ],
+                },
+                select: {
+                  feedback: { select: { personId: true } },
+                  textReply: { select: { personId: true } },
+                },
+              },
+            },
+          },
+        },
+      }),
+      this.client.feedbackSynthesisRun.count({
+        where: { ...scope, status: SynthesisRunStatus.running },
+      }),
+    ])
+    return {
+      summarizing: running > 0,
+      themes: (latest?.themes ?? []).flatMap((theme) => {
+        const people = new Set(
+          theme.members.flatMap((member) => {
+            const personId =
+              member.feedback?.personId ?? member.textReply?.personId
+            return personId === undefined ? [] : [personId]
+          }),
+        ).size
+        return people === 0
+          ? []
+          : [
+              {
+                id: theme.id,
+                title: theme.title,
+                summary: theme.summary,
+                people,
+              },
+            ]
+      }),
+    }
+  }
+
+  // Resolved lazily: importing ContactsModule here closes the module cycle
+  // through Campaigns that organizationTeam.service.ts describes.
+  private resolveContacts(): ContactsService {
+    return this.moduleRef.get(ContactsService, { strict: false })
+  }
+
+  private async respondentsFor(
+    outreach: Outreach,
+    channel: PriorityResultsChannel,
+  ): Promise<SendRespondents> {
+    const base = {
+      outreachId: outreach.id,
+      name: outreach.name,
+      channel,
+      date: (outreach.date ?? outreach.createdAt).toISOString(),
+    }
+    if (channel === 'text') {
+      const reached = await this.client.contactInteractionText.count({
+        where: { outreachId: outreach.id },
+      })
+      // Heard means they said something: a reply that was only STOP is an
+      // opt-out, not an answer on the priority.
+      const replies = await this.client.pollIndividualMessage.findMany({
+        where: {
+          outreachId: outreach.id,
+          sender: PollIndividualMessageSender.CONSTITUENT,
+          NOT: { isOptOut: true },
+        },
+        select: { personId: true },
+        distinct: ['personId'],
+      })
+      const responded = replies.map((reply) => reply.personId)
+      return {
+        send: { ...base, reached, responded: responded.length },
+        respondentIds: responded,
+      }
+    }
+    if (channel === 'phoneBanking' && outreach.phoneBankingListId !== null) {
+      const rows = await this.client.contactInteractionPhoneBanking.findMany({
+        where: { phoneBankingListId: outreach.phoneBankingListId },
+        select: { personId: true, outcome: true },
+      })
+      const reached = new Set(rows.map((row) => row.personId))
+      const responded = [
+        ...new Set(
+          rows
+            .filter((row) => row.outcome === 'answered')
+            .map((row) => row.personId),
+        ),
+      ]
+      return {
+        send: { ...base, reached: reached.size, responded: responded.length },
+        respondentIds: responded,
+      }
+    }
+    if (channel === 'doorKnocking') {
+      // The knock's own envelope, never the turf's stops: a person can sit
+      // in two turfs, and a later CRM knock belongs to no walk.
+      const rows = await this.client.contactInteractionDoorKnock.findMany({
+        where: {
+          organizationSlug: outreach.organizationSlug ?? undefined,
+          outreachId: outreach.id,
+        },
+        select: { personId: true, outcome: true },
+      })
+      const reached = new Set(rows.map((row) => row.personId))
+      const responded = [
+        ...new Set(
+          rows
+            .filter((row) => row.outcome === 'answered')
+            .map((row) => row.personId),
+        ),
+      ]
+      return {
+        send: { ...base, reached: reached.size, responded: responded.length },
+        respondentIds: responded,
+      }
+    }
+    return {
+      send: { ...base, reached: null, responded: null },
+      respondentIds: [],
+    }
+  }
+}

+  householdsIncome25kTo50k: 100,
+  householdsIncome50kTo75k: 100,
+  householdsIncome150kPlus: 100,
+  ...overrides,
+})
+
+const find = (groups: ReturnType<typeof computeRepresentation>, key: string) =>
+  groups.find((group) => group.key === key)
+
+describe('computeRepresentation', () => {
+  it("weights each respondent by their block group's makeup", () => {
+    const renterBlock = counts({ ownerOccupiedHouseholds: 40 })
+    const ownerBlock = counts({ ownerOccupiedHouseholds: 360 })
+
+    const groups = computeRepresentation(counts(), [
+      renterBlock,
+      renterBlock,
+      ownerBlock,
+    ])
+
+    // District: 240/400 own. Respondents: (0.1 + 0.1 + 0.9) / 3 own.
+    expect(find(groups, 'owners')).toMatchObject({
+      districtShare: 0.6,
+      respondentShare: expect.closeTo(1.1 / 3, 5),
+    })
+    expect(find(groups, 'renters')?.respondentShare).toBeCloseTo(1.9 / 3, 5)
+  })
+
+  it('leaves race out until enough people answered', () => {
+    const few = Array.from({ length: MIN_RESPONDENTS_FOR_RACE - 1 }, () =>
+      counts(),
+    )
+    expect(
+      computeRepresentation(counts(), few).some((g) => g.dimension === 'race'),
+    ).toBe(false)
+
+    const enough = [...few, counts()]
+    expect(
+      computeRepresentation(counts(), enough).some(
+        (g) => g.dimension === 'race',
+      ),
+    ).toBe(true)
+  })
+
+  it('drops a race group too small in the district to read', () => {
+    const enough = Array.from({ length: MIN_RESPONDENTS_FOR_RACE }, () =>
+      counts(),
+    )
+    const groups = computeRepresentation(counts(), enough)
+    expect(find(groups, 'nativeAmerican')).toBeUndefined()
+    expect(find(groups, 'black')).toBeDefined()
+  })
+
+  it("drops a whole dimension when one respondent's block group lacks it", () => {
+    const groups = computeRepresentation(counts(), [
+      counts(),
+      counts({ householdsIncomeUniverse: 0 }),
+    ])
+    expect(groups.some((g) => g.dimension === 'income')).toBe(false)
+    expect(groups.some((g) => g.dimension === 'housing')).toBe(true)
+  })
+
+  it('skips a group whose universe is empty rather than dividing by zero', () => {
+    const groups = computeRepresentation(counts({ households: 0 }), [counts()])
+    expect(find(groups, 'owners')).toBeUndefined()
+  })
+})

+
+// The ACS counts gp-data-platform publishes per district
+// (gp_api_district_census_stats, acs_*) and per block group
+// (gp_api_block_group_census_demographics), in camelCase. Both tables carry
+// the same columns, which is what lets a respondent's block group and the
+// district be read as one shape.
+export const ACS_COUNT_KEYS = [
+  'totalPopulation',
+  'populationUnder18',
+  'population65Plus',
+  'populationRaceUniverse',
+  'populationWhiteNh',
+  'populationBlackNh',
+  'populationNativeAmericanNh',
+  'populationAsianNh',
+  'populationOtherNh',

+  'householdsIncome50kTo75k',
+  'householdsIncome75kTo100k',
+  'householdsIncome100kTo150k',
+  'householdsIncome150kPlus',
+] as const
+export type AcsCountKey = (typeof ACS_COUNT_KEYS)[number]
+export type AcsCounts = Record<AcsCountKey, number>
+
+interface GroupDefinition {
+  dimension: RepresentationDimension
+  key: string
+  label: string
+  count: (c: AcsCounts) => number
+  universe: (c: AcsCounts) => number
+}
+
+const ageWorking = (c: AcsCounts): number =>
+  c.totalPopulation - c.populationUnder18 - c.population65Plus
+
+const GROUPS: GroupDefinition[] = [
+  {

+  {
+    dimension: 'housing',
+    key: 'owners',
+    label: 'Own their home',
+    count: (c) => c.ownerOccupiedHouseholds,
+    universe: (c) => c.households,
+  },
+  {
+    dimension: 'housing',
+    key: 'renters',
+    label: 'Rent their home',
+    count: (c) => c.households - c.ownerOccupiedHouseholds,
+    universe: (c) => c.households,
+  },
+  {
+    dimension: 'poverty',
+    key: 'belowPoverty',
+    label: 'Below the poverty line',
+    count: (c) => c.populationBelowPoverty,
+    universe: (c) => c.populationPovertyUniverse,
+  },
+]
+
+// Ethnicity reaches an elected official only as district-wide shares, and
+// only when enough people answered that no one stands out in them.
+export const MIN_RESPONDENTS_FOR_RACE = 25
+// A group this small in the district swings on a handful of people.
+export const MIN_DISTRICT_SHARE_FOR_RACE_GROUP = 0.02
+
+const share = (count: number, universe: number): number | null =>
+  universe > 0 ? Math.max(0, Math.min(1, count / universe)) : null
+
+// Compares the places respondents live with the whole district. Each
+// respondent contributes their block group's composition, so a respondent
+// in a mostly-renter block group counts mostly as a renter: it measures
+// whether outreach reached the right places, not who each person is.
+export const computeRepresentation = (
+  district: AcsCounts,
+  respondentBlockGroups: AcsCounts[],
+): RepresentationGroup[] => {
+  if (respondentBlockGroups.length === 0) return []
+  const showRace = respondentBlockGroups.length >= MIN_RESPONDENTS_FOR_RACE
+  // A dimension shows only when the census has it for every respondent's
+  // block group (a small one can have a figure suppressed). Otherwise two
+  // rows of one dimension would average over different sets of people.
+  const covered = (dimension: RepresentationDimension): boolean =>
+    GROUPS.filter((group) => group.dimension === dimension).every(
+      (group) =>
+        group.universe(district) > 0 &&
+        respondentBlockGroups.every((bg) => group.universe(bg) > 0),
+    )
+  return GROUPS.flatMap((group) => {
+    if (group.dimension === 'race' && !showRace) return []
+    if (!covered(group.dimension)) return []
+    const districtShare = share(group.count(district), group.universe(district))
+    if (districtShare === null) return []
+    if (
+      group.dimension === 'race' &&
+      districtShare < MIN_DISTRICT_SHARE_FOR_RACE_GROUP
+    ) {
+      return []
+    }
+    const respondentShare =
+      respondentBlockGroups.reduce(
+        (sum, bg) => sum + (share(group.count(bg), group.universe(bg)) ?? 0),
+        0,
+      ) / respondentBlockGroups.length
+    return [
+      {
+        dimension: group.dimension,
+        key: group.key,
+        label: group.label,
+        respondentShare,
+        districtShare,
+      },
+    ]
+  })
+}

+import { useEffect, useMemo, useRef } from 'react'
+import maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'
+import { MapboxOverlay } from '@deck.gl/mapbox'
+import { PolygonLayer } from '@deck.gl/layers'
+import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css'
+import { NEXT_PUBLIC_GEOAPIFY_TILES_KEY } from 'appEnv'
+import { boundsOfPoints, toGridCells, type GridCell } from './respondentGrid'
+
+// The contact map's style, so every map in the product reads as one.
+const STYLE_URL = `https://maps.geoapify.com/v1/styles/osm-liberty/style.json?apiKey=${NEXT_PUBLIC_GEOAPIFY_TILES_KEY}`
+const EMPTY_STYLE: maplibregl.StyleSpecification = {
+  version: 8,
+  sources: {},
+  layers: [],
+}
+// `--primary` written out: a deck.gl canvas cannot read a CSS variable.
+const PRIMARY_BLUE: [number, number, number] = [30, 99, 236]
+const FIT_PADDING_PX = 40
+
+// Opacity carries the count, so one hue stays legible over the streets and
+// the busiest square is always the darkest.
+const fillFor = (
+  count: number,
+  max: number,
+): [number, number, number, number] => [
+  ...PRIMARY_BLUE,
+  Math.round(40 + (count / max) * 180),
+]
+
+export const RespondentHeatGrid = ({
+  points,
+}: {
+  points: { lat: number; lng: number }[]
+}) => {
+  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null)
+  const overlayRef = useRef<MapboxOverlay | null>(null)
+  const cells = useMemo(() => toGridCells(points), [points])
+  const bounds = useMemo(() => boundsOfPoints(points), [points])
+
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const container = containerRef.current
+    if (!container) return
+    const map = new maplibregl.Map({
+      container,
+      style: STYLE_URL,
+      attributionControl: false,
+      ...(bounds
+        ? { bounds, fitBoundsOptions: { padding: FIT_PADDING_PX } }
+        : { center: [-98.5, 39.8], zoom: 3 }),
+    })
+    let swapped = false
+    map.on('error', (event) => {
+      const status = (event.error as { status?: number } | undefined)?.status
+      if ((status !== 401 && status !== 403) || swapped) return
+      swapped = true
+      map.setStyle(EMPTY_STYLE)
+    })
+    map.addControl(
+      new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true }),
+      'bottom-right',
+    )
+    map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl({ showCompass: false }))
+    const overlay = new MapboxOverlay({ interleaved: false, layers: [] })
+    map.addControl(overlay)
+    overlayRef.current = overlay
+    return () => {
+      overlayRef.current = null
+      map.remove()
+    }
+  }, [bounds])
+
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const max = cells.reduce((top, cell) => Math.max(top, cell.count), 1)
+    overlayRef.current?.setProps({
+      layers: [
+        new PolygonLayer<GridCell>({
+          id: 'respondent-grid',
+          data: cells,
+          getPolygon: (cell) => cell.polygon,
+          getFillColor: (cell) => fillFor(cell.count, max),
+          getLineColor: [...PRIMARY_BLUE, 120],
+          lineWidthMinPixels: 1,
+          stroked: true,
+          filled: true,
+        }),
+      ],
+    })
+    // bounds: a new map instance has a fresh overlay with no layers on it.
+  }, [cells, bounds])
+
+  return (
+    <div
+      ref={containerRef}
+      className="h-80 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-border"
+    />
+  )
+}

+// About 400m on a side at US latitudes: a few blocks, so one square never
+// stands for one household.
+export const CELL_DEGREES = 0.004
+
+export interface GridCell {
+  polygon: [number, number][]
+  count: number
+}
+
+// Bins respondents into fixed squares. Fixed rather than zoom-dependent so
+// the squares are the same on every screen and a reload never redraws them.
+export const toGridCells = (
+  points: { lat: number; lng: number }[],
+): GridCell[] => {
+  const cells = new Map<string, { row: number; col: number; count: number }>()
+  for (const { lat, lng } of points) {
+    const row = Math.floor(lat / CELL_DEGREES)
+    const col = Math.floor(lng / CELL_DEGREES)
+    const key = `${row}:${col}`
+    const cell = cells.get(key)
+    if (cell) cell.count += 1
+    else cells.set(key, { row, col, count: 1 })
+  }
+  return [...cells.values()].map(({ row, col, count }) => {
+    const south = row * CELL_DEGREES
+    const west = col * CELL_DEGREES
+    const north = south + CELL_DEGREES
+    const east = west + CELL_DEGREES
+    return {
+      count,
+      polygon: [
+        [west, south],
+        [east, south],
+        [east, north],
+        [west, north],
+        [west, south],
+      ],
+    }
+  })
+}
+
+export const boundsOfPoints = (
+  points: { lat: number; lng: number }[],
+): [[number, number], [number, number]] | null => {
+  if (points.length === 0) return null
+  let minLng = Infinity
+  let minLat = Infinity
+  let maxLng = -Infinity
+  let maxLat = -Infinity
+  for (const { lat, lng } of points) {
+    minLng = Math.min(minLng, lng)
+    minLat = Math.min(minLat, lat)
+    maxLng = Math.max(maxLng, lng)
+    maxLat = Math.max(maxLat, lat)
+  }
+  return [
+    [minLng, minLat],
+    [maxLng + CELL_DEGREES, maxLat + CELL_DEGREES],
+  ]
+}

When a theme member has neither a `feedback` nor a `textReply` relation, `member.feedback?.personId ?? member.textReply?.personId` evaluates to `undefined`. JavaScript's `Set` treats `undefined` as a distinct member, so a single `undefined` entry inflates `.size` by 1 for any theme containing such members.

The parallel implementation in `priorityResults.service.ts` guards against this with `.flatMap(...)` and an explicit `undefined` check, and also pre-filters members via a `where` clause requiring at least one relation to be present. This version does neither.
